day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Take the Leonardo Express train to Roma Termini (€14, ~32 min), then connect to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Pick up a local SIM card or activate roaming at the airport.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite near Roma Termini — try a slice of pizza al taglio from a 24-hour bakery or a kebab shop (€3–5). Many spots near Termini stay open late.

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival night simple. Pre-book your Leonardo Express ticket online to save time. Have your accommodation address saved offline. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport if needed, but ATMs in the city offer better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. After a leisurely start, head to the nearby local market or a corner café for breakfast. Then make your way to the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration — book tickets online in advance to skip lines (€16 combo ticket includes Colosseum entry). Spend the morning wandering the ancient ruins of the Forum where Julius Caesar once walked.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your combo ticket access into the Colosseum (included in the €16 ticket). Explore the iconic amphitheater, imagining gladiatorial battles. Afterward, stroll through the Circus Maximus area and enjoy the open-air atmosphere. Stop at a nearby alimentari (deli) for a cheap lunch picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Trastevere neighborhood in the early evening — a 20-minute bus ride. Explore the charming cobblestone streets, street art, and lively piazzas. Enjoy the neighborhood's vibrant nightlife atmosphere without spending much.

meals.breakfast: Café cornetto e cappuccino at a local bar near the hotel (€2–3). Stand at the bar like a local to avoid table service surcharges.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch from a nearby alimentari or Mercato di Testaccio — grab fresh bread, cheese, and cured meats for under €7.
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — a beloved trattoria with authentic Roman dishes like cacio e pepe and carciofi alla romana. Budget €15–20 per person. Arrive early or expect a wait.

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum/Forum/Palatine Hill tickets at coopculture.it at least 2–3 days in advance to avoid sold-out slots. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover several kilometers on uneven ancient stone.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — one of the world's greatest art collections. Book skip-the-line tickets online in advance (€17–20). Arrive right at opening (8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Allow 2–3 hours to explore the galleries, maps room, and culminate in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museums, visit St. Peter's Basilica — entry is FREE. Climb to the top of the dome for panoramic views of Rome (€8 with elevator, €6 by stairs). Spend time in St. Peter's Square people-watching. Head to the Prati neighborhood nearby for an affordable lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Tiber River toward Castel Sant'Angelo for beautiful exterior views (free from outside). Cross the Ponte Sant'Angelo for iconic angel-lined bridge photos. Continue to Piazza Navona — free to visit, great for street performers and atmosphere. End the evening with a gelato.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and espresso at a local bar near the hotel before heading out (€2–3).
meals.lunch: Pizzarium by Gabriele Bonci in Prati — Rome's most famous pizza al taglio spot, sold by weight. Budget €8–12 for a satisfying lunch.
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo near the Vatican — classic Roman trattoria with set-price menus around €15–18 per person including wine. Try trippa alla romana or abbacchio.

day_by_day.notes: Dress code is strictly enforced at St. Peter's Basilica — no bare shoulders or knees. Bring a scarf or light layer. The Vatican is extremely crowded; morning arrival is essential. The free entry to St. Peter's makes this one of Rome's best budget experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery Art Tour — one of Rome's most intimate and world-class galleries housing Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings. IMPORTANT: Reservations are mandatory and entry is timed in 2-hour slots (€15 + €2 booking fee). Book the 9:00 AM slot for the best experience. Afterward, take a relaxing walk through the surrounding Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's version of Central Park, completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Villa Borghese, walk or take a short bus to the Spanish Steps (Piazza di Spagna) — free to visit and great for people-watching. Window-shop along Via Condotti (Rome's luxury street — looking is free!). Walk to the Trevi Fountain (15 min) — toss a coin for good luck (€0.01 or whatever you wish). Visit the nearby Pantheon — entry is now €5 but absolutely worth it for this 2,000-year-old architectural marvel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the historic center around Campo de' Fiori — a lively square that transforms into a bar and social scene in the evenings. Browse the remaining market stalls (market runs until afternoon) and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere. Great spot for affordable aperitivo.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh cornetto and cappuccino at a neighborhood bar (€2–3). Try a cornetto integrale (whole wheat) for something different.
meals.lunch: Forno Campo de' Fiori — a legendary bakery serving incredible pizza bianca and focaccia. Grab lunch for under €6. Eat standing or find a spot in the piazza.
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Lucia in Trastevere — a no-frills, cash-only Roman classic. Try rigatoni alla pajata or spaghetti all'amatriciana. Budget €14–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets sell out weeks in advance — book as early as possible at galleriaborghese.it. The gallery only admits 360 visitors per 2-hour session, making it an exclusive and uncrowded experience. Bring your booking confirmation printed or on your phone.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Aventine Hill — a peaceful, less-touristy neighborhood with stunning views. Visit the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for a free panoramic view of Rome and St. Peter's dome. Then find the famous Knights of Malta Keyhole (Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta) — peek through the keyhole for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's Basilica. Completely free and magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's true foodie district. Visit the Testaccio Market (Mercato di Testaccio) for a deep dive into Roman food culture. Browse stalls selling fresh produce, cheese, and street food. Explore the nearby Non-Catholic Cemetery (€3 suggested donation) where Keats and Shelley are buried — a surprisingly moving and beautiful spot.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely evening passeggiata (stroll) along Via del Corso or around Piazza del Popolo — a grand twin-church piazza with free entry. Watch the Roman evening ritual of families and friends strolling and socializing. End the night with an aperitivo hour (typically 6–8 PM) where many bars offer free snacks with your drink.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local forno (bakery) in the Testaccio area for fresh-baked goods (€2–4).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Testaccio Market food stalls — try supplì (fried rice balls, €2 each), fresh pasta, or a trapizzino (pizza pocket sandwich, €3–4). Budget €8–10 total.
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — a beloved neighborhood restaurant built into Monte dei Cocci (a hill of ancient amphora shards). Authentic Roman cuisine, budget €15–20 per person. Try the rigatoni con la pajata.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market is open Monday–Saturday until about 2:00 PM — plan your afternoon timing accordingly. The Aventine Hill is a short walk or bus ride from most central areas. Wear comfortable shoes as the hill has some steep sections.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the lesser-known but spectacular Capitoline Museums (Musei Capitolini) — the world's oldest public museums, housing Marcus Aurelius's original bronze equestrian statue, Capitoline Wolf sculpture, and stunning views of the Roman Forum from the terrace (€15, free for EU citizens under 18). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the hilltop complex designed by Michelangelo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Circus Maximus and then explore the Mouth of Truth (Bocca della Verità) at Santa Maria in Cosmedin church — free entry, small donation appreciated. A fun photo opportunity made famous by Roman Holiday. Stroll through the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood — one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric districts with beautiful ruins integrated into the urban fabric.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the city center for a final sunset view from the Pincian Hill Terrace in Villa Borghese — completely free and one of Rome's most romantic viewpoints overlooking Piazza del Popolo. End the evening with a final Roman dinner in the Monti neighborhood — Rome's hipster village with great value restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel — espresso and pastry (€2–3). Try a maritozzo (cream-filled bun) if you haven't yet — a Roman specialty.
meals.lunch: Grab street food near the Jewish Ghetto — try carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes, €4–6) from a street vendor or casual café. A uniquely Roman-Jewish culinary tradition.
meals.dinner: Trattoria Monti — a cozy Monti neighborhood gem known for regional Italian cuisine from Le Marche. Budget €18–22 per person. Try the vincisgrassi (regional lasagna) or any fresh pasta dish.

day_by_day.notes: The Capitoline Museums offer a free day on the first Sunday of each month — if Day 6 falls on that date, take advantage! Check the museum website for current free admission dates. The Jewish Ghetto restaurants are also excellent for dinner if you want to stay in that area.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the hotel and store luggage at the front desk or a luggage storage service (Stow Your Bags near Termini, ~€6/bag). Take a final morning walk through whichever neighborhood you loved most. Visit any missed churches — Rome's churches are largely free and house incredible art (try Santa Maria Maggiore, San Giovanni in Laterano, or San Clemente with its underground layers).
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Campo de' Fiori market or Via della Croce — avoid tourist trap shops near major monuments. Look for local ceramics, food products (truffle oil, pasta, biscotti), or prints of Roman artwork. Head to Roma Termini to collect luggage and catch transport to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Rome. Reflect on an incredible week of art, history, and food in the Eternal City.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast at a local bar — make it special with a sit-down cappuccino and fresh cornetto (€4–6 with table service as a farewell treat).
meals.lunch: Quick and satisfying lunch near Termini — try Mercato Centrale Roma inside Termini station, a gourmet food hall with artisan vendors. Budget €10–15 for a quality final meal.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal, or grab a panino and snacks from a Termini food shop for the journey (€5–8).

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transport and security. The Leonardo Express from Termini to Fiumicino takes 32 minutes and costs €14. Alternatively, bus FL1 is cheaper (€8) but slower. Keep your transit ticket for the entire journey as inspectors do check. Luggage storage at Termini is available at Kipoint or Radical Storage for ~€6 per bag per day.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — no morning activities scheduled. Flight UA arrives at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival day — no afternoon activities scheduled. Use travel time to rest.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Leonardo Express train or a pre-booked taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and unwind. Pick up a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or hotel bar if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Light snack at the hotel bar or a quick bite near the resort upon arrival — keep it simple after a long travel day.

day_by_day.notes: Do not over-plan Day 1. Priority is a smooth arrival and a good night's sleep. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance since you arrive late. Pre-download the Roma Pass app and Google Maps offline for Rome to prepare for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start — enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast, then take a gentle orientation walk around your neighborhood to get your bearings. Head toward the historic center and visit the iconic Trevi Fountain and the Pantheon on foot, soaking in Rome's stunning street-level architecture without rushing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Borghese Gallery Art Tour — Visit this intimate world-class gallery housing Bernini's breathtaking sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic masterpieces. Book tickets well in advance as entry is timed and strictly limited to 2-hour slots. The gallery sits inside the beautiful Villa Borghese park, perfect for a post-visit stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the elegant Pincian Hill terrace for panoramic sunset views over Rome. Then head to the Prati neighborhood near Castel Sant'Angelo for dinner — a lively area with excellent mid-range trattorias.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bar — enjoy a classic Roman cornetto with cappuccino (€3–5).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Pantheon — try Osteria dell'Ingegno or grab a slice of pizza al taglio from a local forno (€8–12).
meals.dinner: Trattoria dei Gracchi or Il Sorpasso in Prati — hearty Roman pasta dishes like cacio e pepe or amatriciana (€25–35 per person with wine).

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets must be booked online in advance — check gebart.it. Comfortable walking shoes are essential. The gallery is a 15-minute walk through Villa Borghese park from the Spagna metro stop.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Arrive early (pre-booked skip-the-line tickets are a must) to beat the crowds. Spend 3–4 hours exploring one of the world's greatest art collections, from the Gallery of Maps to Raphael's Rooms, culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museums, visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry) and climb the dome for sweeping views over Rome if energy permits. Then cross the Tiber and explore the lively Borgo neighborhood. Rest your feet at a café before continuing.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Wander the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling local Roman street food including supplì, artichokes, and local wines. This guided evening experience perfectly blends neighborhood atmosphere with authentic Roman flavors.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a quick bar stop near the Vatican — cornetto and espresso to fuel the museum visit.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near St. Peter's Square — Pizzarium Bonci (a short taxi away in Prati) is legendary for creative pizza al taglio (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk experience, or finish with a sit-down meal at Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — beloved local trattoria (€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets should be booked weeks in advance at museivaticani.va. Dress code applies — cover shoulders and knees for the Sistine Chapel. The Trastevere walk typically runs in the evening (19:00–22:00) — confirm exact timing when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Cooking Class — Begin at Mercato Testaccio, Rome's most authentic food market, to source fresh seasonal ingredients alongside a local chef. Learn about Roman culinary traditions before heading to a nearby kitchen to prepare a hands-on Roman meal including pasta, antipasti, and dessert.
day_by_day.afternoon: After your cooking class lunch, walk off the meal exploring the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's original working-class 'rione' with excellent street art and the iconic Pyramid of Cestius. Visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery, a surprisingly beautiful and peaceful spot.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening — visit the vibrant Ostiense neighborhood for aperitivo hour (Spritz and nibbles), then enjoy a casual dinner at one of the area's trendy osterie.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a neighborhood bar before heading to Testaccio.
meals.lunch: Included in the Testaccio Cooking Class — you eat what you cook!
meals.dinner: Osteria Fernanda or Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — authentic Roman cuisine in a casual setting (€20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Cooking Class typically runs morning to early afternoon (9:00–13:00). Book through a reputable provider like Eating Italy Food Tours or Cookly. Testaccio is easily reachable by metro (Piramide station, Line B) or tram.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration — Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire, exploring the ruins of the Forum where Julius Caesar once walked, and climb Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the ruins. The Colosseum combo ticket covers all three sites — arrive early to avoid peak heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Colosseum (included in combo ticket) — book a timed entry in advance. Afterward, explore the Celio neighborhood nearby and discover the lesser-visited Basilica di San Clemente, which features stunning medieval mosaics and layers of history descending underground.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Monti neighborhood — Rome's hipster village — for an evening of aperitivo, boutique browsing, and dinner. The area has excellent mid-range restaurants and a wonderful local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a bar near the Colosseum area.
meals.lunch: Packed snack or a quick stop at a nearby alimentari — avoid overpriced tourist restaurants immediately around the Colosseum.
meals.dinner: Trattoria Monti or Ai Tre Scalini in Monti neighborhood — excellent regional Italian cuisine in a cozy setting (€25–35 per person with wine).

day_by_day.notes: Colosseum + Roman Forum + Palatine Hill combo tickets must be booked in advance at coopculture.it. The full site visit can take 4–5 hours — wear sun protection and bring water as there is little shade. Comfortable walking shoes essential.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning to revisit a favorite neighborhood or explore somewhere new. Consider the Campo de' Fiori morning market (open until ~14:00) for fresh produce, flowers, and local color. Stroll to nearby Piazza Navona and admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Capitoline Museums (Musei Capitolini) — the world's oldest public museums, housing incredible classical sculpture including the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and stunning views over the Roman Forum from the terrace. A perfect art-focused afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge-worthy farewell dinner at a slightly elevated mid-range restaurant. The Trastevere or Prati neighborhoods offer excellent options. Enjoy a post-dinner gelato walk along the Tiber riverbank — a quintessential Roman evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café near Campo de' Fiori — try Forno Campo de' Fiori for exceptional pizza bianca and pastries.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a trattoria near Piazza Navona — try Osteria dell'Anima or a nearby pizzeria (€15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Pagliaccio (splurge option) or a well-reviewed trattoria in Trastevere such as Tonnarello — enjoy Roman classics and a bottle of local wine (€35–50 per person for a special evening).

day_by_day.notes: Capitoline Museums are open Tuesday–Sunday. Book tickets online at museicapitolini.org to avoid queues. Saturday evenings in Rome are lively — book dinner reservations in advance. Gelato recommendation: Fatamorgana or Fior di Luna in Trastevere.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — enjoy a slow breakfast and pack. If time allows, revisit a favorite spot or explore a neighborhood you missed. Sunday mornings are magical in Rome — quieter streets, church bells, and locals at their leisurely best. Consider attending Mass at a beautiful church like Santa Maria Maggiore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, enjoy a final Roman lunch at a neighborhood trattoria. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping — the Monti neighborhood has excellent independent shops for artisan goods, prints, and food products to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport or train station. The Leonardo Express from Roma Termini to Fiumicino Airport takes 32 minutes and runs every 15–30 minutes — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Final Italian breakfast — sit at a proper bar and savor a perfect cappuccino and cornetto one last time (€3–5).
meals.lunch: Last Roman meal — keep it classic. Cacio e pepe or carbonara at a trusted trattoria. Budget €15–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner if departing in the evening, or an early dinner before transfer — keep it light and practical.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late departure. Confirm airport transfer in advance. The Leonardo Express is the most reliable option to Fiumicino; taxis are metered and cost approximately €48–55 fixed rate from central Rome.

day_by_day.evening: Join the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — a guided twilight stroll through cobblestone streets sampling supplì, cured meats, pecorino, artisan wines, and Roman street food. Conclude the evening with a nightcap at a rooftop bar overlooking the illuminated city.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a packed pastry box and thermos of espresso for an early Borghese start
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Caffè delle Arti inside the Borghese gardens — a charming terrace café perfect for salads, bruschetta, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: The Trastevere Food & Wine Walk serves as a progressive dinner — supplemented by a final sit-down dessert course at Tonnarello or Grazia & Graziella in Trastevere

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery is one of Rome's most sought-after tickets — book 3–4 weeks in advance minimum. The evening walk typically runs 3 hours; wear comfortable shoes. Ask your guide to include a stop at a local wine bar for a premium Lazio wine tasting.

day_by_day.morning: Start at Rome's most authentic food market — Testaccio Market (Mercato Testaccio) — for the Testaccio Market & Cooking Class experience. Browse stalls of seasonal produce, aged cheeses, fresh pasta, and local specialties with your chef guide. Then head to a nearby culinary studio for a hands-on cooking class: make fresh pasta, Roman sauces, and a classic dolce from scratch.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, take a private car to the Colosseum and Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration. A private archaeologist guide walks you through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire — the Forum where Julius Caesar walked, the Arch of Titus, and the sweeping ruins of Palatine Hill with its imperial palace remains and stunning city views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a terrace bar near the Circus Maximus, then a premium dinner reservation at one of Rome's finest restaurants — a true fine-dining experience to celebrate the midpoint of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Light in-hotel breakfast before heading to Testaccio early (market is best before 11am)
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class — a full Roman feast prepared by your own hands, paired with local wines selected by the chef
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aroma Restaurant (rooftop of Palazzo Manfredi, overlooking the Colosseum) — one of Rome's most spectacular dining experiences with a Michelin-starred menu

day_by_day.notes: Book Aroma Restaurant well in advance — it is one of Rome's most iconic and in-demand fine dining venues. The cooking class typically runs 3–4 hours including the meal. Request a gluten-free or dietary-adjusted menu if needed.

day_by_day.morning: A relaxed morning — sleep in and enjoy a long, leisurely hotel breakfast. Then take a private guided walk through the historic center: Pantheon (free entry, arrive early), Piazza Navona, and the Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi. Explore the baroque grandeur at your own pace with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Doria Pamphilj Gallery — a hidden gem palazzo housing one of Rome's finest private art collections including Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X. Afterward, browse the luxury boutiques of Via del Corso or enjoy a private fashion styling session arranged by the hotel concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at Salotto 42, a sophisticated lounge overlooking the Temple of Hadrian. Follow with dinner at a celebrated contemporary Roman restaurant for a modern interpretation of traditional cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — take your time, request eggs Benedict or a Roman-style frittata with seasonal vegetables
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante La Rosetta near the Pantheon — Rome's premier seafood restaurant, beloved by locals and visiting dignitaries alike
meals.dinner: Dinner at Retrobottega or All'Oro — avant-garde Roman cuisine with exceptional tasting menus and wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon now charges a small admission fee — the hotel concierge can arrange skip-the-line access. Salotto 42 is ideal for golden-hour drinks; arrive by 7pm to secure a terrace seat. The Doria Pamphilj audio guide narrated by the Pamphilj family themselves is a charming touch.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip option: Private car to Ostia Antica — Rome's remarkably preserved ancient port city, far less crowded than Pompeii and equally impressive. Explore the ancient theater, mosaic floors, and bathhouses with a private archaeologist guide. Alternatively, a morning visit to the Capitoline Museums for world-class ancient Roman sculpture and the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Rome for a leisurely afternoon. Indulge in a luxury spa treatment at the hotel or a premium day spa in the city center. Then visit the Trevi Fountain (best in the late afternoon when light is golden) and toss your coin for good luck.
day_by_day.evening: A grand farewell-to-Rome dinner at a celebrated restaurant — choose a rooftop venue or a historic palazzo setting for maximum atmosphere. Conclude the evening with a private after-hours visit to a wine cellar for a curated Italian wine tasting with a sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — request a packed luxury picnic basket if taking the Ostia Antica day trip
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch among the ruins of Ostia Antica (prepared by the hotel) or, if staying in Rome, lunch at Pierluigi in Piazza de' Ricci — a beloved Roman institution with excellent seafood
meals.dinner: Dinner at Il Pagliaccio (two Michelin stars) or Imàgo at Hotel Hassler — panoramic rooftop views and extraordinary tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Ostia Antica is approximately 45 minutes from central Rome by private car. The site is less visited than the Roman Forum and offers an extraordinary immersive experience. Book the private sommelier wine tasting through the hotel concierge — a wonderful way to bring home knowledge of Italian wine regions.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a last morning stroll — perhaps to a nearby neighborhood market or a quiet piazza for one last espresso at a local bar, standing at the counter like a true Roman. Pick up artisan gifts: aged pecorino, truffle products, or a bottle of Brunello di Montalcino from a specialty enoteca.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure time, the concierge can arrange a final lunch at a nearby restaurant or a gourmet farewell meal at the hotel. Private luxury transfer to Fiumicino Airport — allow ample time for international departures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Rome. Carry the memories of seven extraordinary days of art, food, history, and la dolce vita.

meals.breakfast: Final full hotel breakfast — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Supplì Roma (casual, iconic Roman street food for a nostalgic send-off) or a sit-down meal at Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio if time allows
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge at Fiumicino (Sala Michelangelo lounge recommended for premium travelers)

day_by_day.notes: Check-out is typically at noon — request a late check-out (2pm) through the concierge if your flight allows. Keep one small bag accessible for last-minute shopping. The hotel can arrange gift wrapping and secure packaging for fragile items like wine or ceramics purchased during the trip. Confirm private transfer booking the night before.

query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June 2026 from Chicago
